headlines.article_text: CoreWeave CEO cancels planned share sale program Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said Wednesday that he has canceled his 10b5 stock sale plan. Intrator has sold 8.26 million shares at an average price of $96.14 per share for a total of $794.2 million under his most recent plan. The neocloud beat on revenue in Q3 and upped its forecast, while Intrator indicated the company will be fine despite last week's Democratic midterm sweep. In this article CRWV Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Michael Intrator, co-founder and chief executive officer of CoreWeave Inc., at the Bloomberg Tech summit in London, UK, on Tuesday, Oct. 21, 2025. Chris J. Ratcliffe | Bloomberg | Getty Images CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC on Wednesday that he has canceled his 10b5 stock sale plan after the company reported strong revenue growth and beat Q3 expectations. "Until there is a material change in in, in our equity pricing, my 10b5 has been sidelined," he told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." He said any further selling would be "just normal tax stuff." Under Intrator's 10b5-1 plan announced in November 2025, the CEO has sold 8.26 million shares at an average price of $96.14 per share for a total of $794.2 million. Intrator and his co-founders have faced criticism for their stock sales as the company's stock has struggled, with shares down 18% so far in 2026 despite a 20% post-earnings rally on Wednesday. The company has faced further pressure from the sell-off in the aftermath of last week's sweeping electoral victory for Democrats, but Intrator told investors on the earnings call that the company isn't worried about the political changes on the horizon. "We do not anticipate any impact from the seismic regulatory shift that's occurred," Intrator said on his company's earnings call late Tuesday, in response to a question about new pressures after the election. "We believe that what has occurred is a statement around how you build. We want to build responsibly." Intrator's comments came after CoreWeave reported 168% year-over-year revenue growth, beating estimates, and lifted its forecast for 2026. The stock rallied in extended trading, as the report offered some relief to investors, who have pushed the shares down about 27% over the past month. But CoreWeave says it's not slowing down. The company said it still anticipates 1.85 gigawatts in active power by the end of 2026, and it's now targeting $37 billion to $39 billion in full-year capital expenditures, implying 155% growth at the middle of the range. "We are very comfortable with our pipeline," Intrator said, adding that the message from voters isn't a deterrent because the company is always conscious about "being good neighbors." "We think that that is an opportunity for us to continue to scale our business within the new political reality that exists," Intrator said. —CNBC's Nick Wells contributed to this article. headlines.article_text: CFTC investigates if Kalshi improperly self-certified event contracts Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Kalshi called it a minor issue in how the contracts were filed and said it is working with the CFTC to address the matter. Prediction market platforms are allowed to self-certify event contracts without the federal agency's approval, as long as they comply with the Commodity Exchange Act. A Kalshi billboard displaying US Congress midterm election odds in New York, US, on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. Angelina Katsanis | Bloomberg | Getty Images The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is investigating if prediction market platform Kalshi failed to properly inform the agency of proposed event contracts, Kalshi confirmed to CNBC. Kalshi called it a minor issue in how the contracts were filed and said it is working with the CFTC to address the matter. The CFTC flagged weather-related contracts, Kalshi said. The leading prediction market platform didn't say when the agency began investigating Kalshi. The CFTC didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Politico first reported on the probe on Tuesday, noting charges could happen soon, based on the CFTC's private notification to Kalshi. The platform declined to comment on any possible charges. Prediction market platforms are allowed to self-certify event contracts without the federal agency's prior approval, as long as they comply with the Commodity Exchange Act. The self-regulation allows for faster introduction of new contracts. 'Procedural error' "The notice is about a procedural error involving the submission of a handful of contracts, many of which weren't live," said Elisabeth Diana, head of communications at Kalshi. "We are already addressing the issue." The move is the latest by the CFTC as it seeks to rein in prediction markets, which face growing scrutiny in Washington D.C. from regulators and members of Congress . In August, the CFTC ordered Kalshi to take down sports-related " mention markets " — where speculators can trade on what individuals will say in a broadcast or speech — while it looked into the event contract type. The agency is also conducting a broad probe into competitor Polymarket , which includes reviewing if the company violated a 2022 settlement with the CFTC to prohibit U.S. traders from accessing its international trading platform. Polymarket's domestic exchange operates separately from the global platform. Prediction markets are also expected to face heightened scrutiny once the Democratic Congress is sworn into office in January. Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., in a Tuesday social media post on X , called for a ban on sports prediction markets — which account for the overwhelming majority of volume on leading platforms.
